audit.whatIsWrong: Cell Division is described as 'when he takes damage he drops four pieces that heal him'. Riot's text splits that into two separate mechanics: he sheds a reabsorbable healing chunk each time he HITS an enemy with an ability, and separately, on taking fatal damage he splits into 4 bloblets and revives if any survive. The page also credits Unstable Matter with CC ('Q/W CC', 'Q/W slows', 'W bounce') — W is percent-max-health magic damage on a 5s cooldown with no crowd control at all. This matches the mirror's finding that W is his damage, not his defence.
audit.why: The denial plan is the win condition here, and it is aimed at the wrong trigger: chunks appear when he lands abilities, not when he is hit. And a player who thinks W will peel him off will hold Ragnarok for an ability that cannot stop him.
audit.corrected: Stand on the chunks he sheds when he lands abilities; killing him spawns 4 bloblets that revive him. His CC is Q's grab and E's knock-up — W has none.

audit.whatIsWrong: Elastic Slingshot is the tracked ability of the whole page with no cooldown given anywhere.
audit.why: 21/18/15/12/9s is the widest punish window in the matchup — over 20 seconds at rank 1, closing to 9s by late, which is exactly why he is free food in lane and a real engage tool in teamfights.
audit.corrected: Elastic Slingshot 21s at rank 1, 9s maxed; Stretching Strikes 14s at rank 1; Unstable Matter 5s; Let's Bounce 120s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart marks Levels 1, 4-5 and 6 as Skill and gives Olaf two-plus items, while whys[0] says Olaf wins first contact outright, whys[4] says Ragnarok answers his CC, and whys[6] and spikes[3] say Zac reclaims the two-item window.
audit.why: On a 55.13% lane the early rows are Olaf's and the late row is not; the chart currently has both backwards.
audit.corrected: Olaf Levels 1 through first item; Skill at two-plus items.

audit.why: Mirror confirms Ragnarok is immunity to disables for as long as he keeps attacking, 100s at rank 1, and that Undertow cuts armour as well as speed. Both are stated consistently here, and the ratings stay inverse to the mirror's side.

edits.after: Short trades favour your passive life steal over his chunk recovery once you stand on the pieces.

edits.after: Ragnarok answers his Q grab and E knock-up — Unstable Matter has no CC at all to stop the dive.

edits.after: Ragnarok answers his Q grab and E knock-up, and Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1 — bait it, then dive.

edits.before: Zac's biggest threat: at 2+ items his long-range E engage and AOE CC let him peel for his carries while your flat true damage scales down.
edits.after: Zac's biggest threat: at 2+ items Elastic Slingshot is down to 9s, so his engage and Let's Bounce peel for his carries every fight.

edits.before: Zac is an off-meta top with no early kill threat on you, and you own first contact: Q-slow into auto, then your passive ramps attack speed as you trade. The key is his passive blobs — when he takes damage he drops four pieces that heal him if he picks them up, so stand on them or walk them off and he gets nothing back. At 2-3 you have Q plus E, a guaranteed true-damage burst he simply can't match while his only sustain is the blobs you're denying.
edits.after: Zac is an off-meta top with no early kill threat on you, and you own first contact: Undertow into autos, then your passive ramps attack speed as you trade. The key is Cell Division — every time he lands an ability he sheds a chunk that heals him if he collects it, so stand on the chunks and he gets nothing back. At 2-3 Undertow plus Reckless Swing is a true-damage burst he can't match while the sustain he needs is under your feet.

edits.before: This is your takeover. Bait his E knock-up or W bounce, then when his CC is committed you E in, Q-slow to stick him, and W-omnivamp out-heals anything he does back. At 6 Ragnarok is the dagger — it cleanses his E knock-up and Q/W slows and makes you unstoppable, so he can't peel himself or kite away when you all-in or dive. With Black Cleaver and Bramble your true damage cuts straight through his stacked HP.
edits.after: This is your takeover. Bait Elastic Slingshot — 21s at rank 1 — and once it is gone you walk in, Undertow to stick him, and let W's shield eat his answer. At 6 Ragnarok is the dagger: it answers his Q grab and the E knock-up, and Unstable Matter carries no CC at all, so nothing peels you off him. With Black Cleaver and Bramble your true damage cuts straight through his stacked HP.

edits.before: You win the lane hard, but Zac's value flips at 2+ items: his long-range E becomes a teamfight engage and his Q/W AOE CC peels for his carries, while your flat true damage and short-fight kit lose punch against full builds. So cash your lead now — take plates, dive him off Ragnarok, and force objectives before the game becomes a teamfight where his disruption matters more than your duel.
edits.after: You win the lane hard, but Zac's value flips at 2+ items: Elastic Slingshot becomes a teamfight engage on a 9s cooldown and Let's Bounce knocks up everyone it lands on, while your flat true damage and short-fight kit lose punch against full builds. So cash your lead now — take plates, dive him off Ragnarok, and force objectives before the game becomes a teamfight where his disruption beats your duel.

notes: Mirror (zac__olaf) was reused rather than re-researched: its three mechanical findings — Ragnarok's 'as long as he keeps attacking' clause at 100s, Unstable Matter being percent-health damage rather than defence, and Undertow cutting armour as well as speed — are restated here from Olaf's side, and the stage winners are kept inverse to it. The kit flags Elastic Slingshot with 'grounding'; Riot's description is only a launch forward, so no grounding claim was made.
